authority: User explicitly requested faster in-place software iteration without shutting down the GPU.
decision: After V19's preflight and single checkpoint transfer pass, stop the one-shot host driver without deleting the VM. Run the unchanged V19 scientific arm through the retained-instance recovery driver, retrieve and hash its artifact, and retain the instance, derived image, and checkpoint for the next preregistered arm when that arm can begin within ten minutes.
unchanged: V19 model, checkpoint, runtime, dtype, kernels, serving flags, workloads, quality gate, SLO, telemetry, economics, timeout, and artifact contract.
orchestration_change: Recovery driver --reuse-staged-runtime-and-checkpoint avoids placement, image build, and transfer; --keep-instance-after-result skips deletion only after a hash-retrieved typed result. Untyped errors still open the bounded repair window.
budget: No cap increase. The original V19 absolute $1.10 and 4,500-second allocation limits remain in force; any follow-up receives its own preregistration and spend attribution.
cleanup: A final owner must retrieve/hash all arm evidence, delete the instance and managed disk, and verify GET not-found plus zero inventories. The existing absolute-deadline watchdog remains active as a fail-safe.
